description: Expected results for the official dfnWorks example examples/graph_transport (lanl/dfnWorks git 821d476, pydfnworks 2.10.0, DFNGen 2.3): 3 elliptical TPL fracture families in a 400x50x50 m domain, graph-based flow left->right (2 MPa -> 1 MPa) and graph particle tracking of 10,000 particles. inputs/driver.py is the unmodified official file. The repo ships no reference outputs for this example, so values were recorded from real runs on this server: three clean runs gave identical values (network seed = pydfnworks default 1; each particle is seeded by its own number).

numeric_checks.name: fractures_accepted
numeric_checks.why: DFNGen accepted fractures before isolated ones are removed (311+315+316)

numeric_checks.name: fractures_final
numeric_checks.why: fractures kept in the final network

numeric_checks.name: final_p32
numeric_checks.why: total fracture intensity P32 (m2/m3) after removal; three families aim at 0.25 each

numeric_checks.name: graph_edges
numeric_checks.why: edges in the intersection graph written to graph_flow.hdf5 (read with KI parse tool)

numeric_checks.name: edge_flow_rate_mean_m3s
numeric_checks.why: mean edge volume flow rate from the graph pressure solve (KI parse tool)

numeric_checks.name: edge_velocity_max_ms
numeric_checks.why: largest edge velocity from the graph flow solve (KI parse tool)

numeric_checks.name: travel_time_min_s
numeric_checks.why: first arrival: smallest particle travel time

numeric_checks.name: travel_time_max_s
numeric_checks.why: last arrival: largest particle travel time

numeric_checks.name: pathline_length_mean_m
numeric_checks.why: mean particle path length (domain is 400 m long in x)

numeric_checks.name: beta_mean_s_per_m
numeric_checks.why: mean Beta (s/m), the transport resistance used for matrix diffusion

reference: own runs (no official reference outputs ship with this example)
notes: Counts must match exactly. Float tolerance is relative 1e-6 (runs repeat exactly; the small slack only allows for other numpy/scipy builds). Matrix diffusion is off in this example, so advective time equals total travel time.
